settings.title: Ramka settings
settings.not_configured_how: To add it, set `{input}` in `domosenso/ramka.inputs.yaml`, then run `domosenso render ramka` and deploy.
settings.render_time_how: From `domosenso/ramka.inputs.yaml`: a change needs a render and a deploy.
settings.all_off: Every page of the rotation is switched off: the tablet shows the first one.
settings.page_off: Switched off: the tablet leaves this view out.
settings.preview_classic: Classic: the now-playing card draws its own wave.
settings.reset_confirm: Set this page's settings back to their defaults?
settings.reset_all: Reset every setting to its default
settings.reset_all_confirm: Set every Ramka setting back to its default?
settings.calibration_procedure: Put a reference meter next to the board and play steady pink noise or music at a talking level. Read both: the measured offset is the reference minus the board's level without offset. Enter it below with a note, then apply it.
settings.calibration_apply_confirm: Write the measured offset and the note into the selected board?
settings.music_template_custom_purpose: Your own profile; starts as today's design.
settings.music_template_custom_best: Anything, once you have tuned it.
settings.music_template_custom_why: When no template fits. Every profile keeps its own values, so tuning one never changes another.
settings.music_template_behind_speakers_purpose: Look like your listening position does.
settings.music_template_behind_speakers_best: Music and TV with the sensor behind or near the speakers, or on the amplifier.
settings.music_template_behind_speakers_why: Undoes the difference you measured between the sensor's spot and your listening position (the home's behind_speakers EQ, or the fitted one once calibrated); flat until you set one.
settings.music_template_lively_why: WLED-MM's fast limiter (50 / 300 ms): a quick attack and release. Expect flicker on quiet material.
settings.music_template_calm_why: WLED's "Lazy" for strong dynamics: a 4.2 s decay keeps loud passages from jumping.
settings.music_template_analyser_best: Watching the sound itself; best with the `bars` or `afterglow` flavour.
settings.music_template_analyser_why: Instant attack and a short release, like the MSGEQ7 spectrum analysers sold on AliExpress and broadcast peak meters.
settings.music_eq_flat_purpose: No correction: the bands as the sensor hears them.
settings.music_eq_flat_best: A sensor at the listening position, or a starting point before you tune.
settings.music_eq_flat_why: When the sensor hears what you hear there is nothing to undo; every other preset starts from here.
settings.music_eq_behind_speakers_purpose: Undoes what the sensor's spot adds compared with your listening position.
settings.music_eq_behind_speakers_best: The sensor behind or close to the speakers, or on the amplifier.
settings.music_eq_behind_speakers_why: Close to a speaker and a wall the bass is several dB louder and the treble differs; the home's own measured curve, set in the input music_eq_presets, takes that back.
settings.music_eq_half_match_best: When the full correction looks dull, or the sensor sits between the speakers and the listening position.
settings.music_eq_half_match_why: A near-field curve measured from one clip varies from run to run; half of it keeps some of the punch of hearing the speakers directly. Set in music_eq_presets.
settings.music_eq_wled_big_speakers_purpose: WLED-MM's frequency profile for an INMP441 microphone near big speakers with strong bass, in six ranges.
settings.music_eq_wled_big_speakers_best: Bass-heavy music on large speakers or with a subwoofer.
settings.music_eq_wled_big_speakers_why: Big speakers flood the low bands; the profile cuts sub, bass and low mids and lifts the treble a little, so the whole spectrum moves.
settings.music_eq_wled_big_speakers_ics_purpose: WLED-MM's "ICS-43434 – big speakers" frequency profile, in six ranges.
settings.music_eq_wled_big_speakers_ics_best: Large speakers; a microphone with a flat response like the ICS-43434.
settings.music_eq_wled_big_speakers_ics_why: Like the INMP441 profile it takes weight out of the bass and lifts the presence; the very top it leaves slightly lower, as the profile does.
settings.music_eq_wled_pink_purpose: WLED's pink-noise correction: the treble lifted against the bass.
settings.music_eq_wled_pink_best: Music with cymbals, hi-hats and synths whose top end should show.
settings.music_eq_wled_pink_why: Music has less energy in the treble than in the bass, so the upper bands look dim; WLED's pink-noise multipliers lift them, here as a gentle rise to +4 dB at the top.
settings.music_eq_bass_light_purpose: Less sub and bass, the rest unchanged.
settings.music_eq_bass_light_best: A sensor near a subwoofer, a wall or a corner; bass-heavy music.
settings.music_eq_bass_light_why: Near walls and corners the bass is several dB louder and the low bands fill the picture; this takes 6–8 dB off them.
settings.music_eq_voices_purpose: Brings out the speech range: mids and presence up, bass down.
settings.music_eq_voices_best: TV, films, podcasts and vocal music.
settings.music_eq_voices_why: Voices sit between about 300 Hz and 4 kHz, their consonants at 2–4 kHz; less bass keeps music beds and explosions from drowning them.
settings.music_eq_sparkle_purpose: Treble detail: presence and air up, a little less bass.
settings.music_eq_sparkle_best: Acoustic music, jazz and classical, and quiet listening.
settings.music_eq_sparkle_why: High frequencies carry little energy and a room microphone loses them with distance; the lift makes strings, cymbals and breath visible.
settings.music_eq_fitted_purpose: Your calibrated curve: the EQ that makes pink noise look level at the sensor's spot.
settings.music_eq_fitted_best: After a pink-noise calibration (see the README).
settings.music_eq_fitted_why: It corrects the microphone, the room and the placement together; set in music_eq_presets, flat until then.
settings.music_eq_curve_unset: flat until the home sets it (input music_eq_presets)
settings.language_how: Each language is its own Ramka dashboard: {paths}. The tablet shows the language of the dashboard it opens: the default dashboard in the tablet user's profile, or the Companion app's start page. A switch on this page follows once it has been tested on a tablet.
settings.calendar_by_url_how: No account login needed: [an ICS link](/config/integrations/dashboard/add?domain=remote_calendar) (Remote calendar, refreshed once a day) or [a CalDAV account](/config/integrations/dashboard/add?domain=caldav) (server URL, user and app password, refreshed every 15 minutes). Then put the new `calendar.*` entity into `calendar` in `domosenso/ramka.inputs.yaml`, run `domosenso render ramka` and deploy.
settings.photo_albums_how: The photo series come from the ticked albums, the top-level folders of the photo folder. With All albums ticked they come from every album and the ticks wait, greyed out, for it to be unticked; none ticked is all of them too. The list follows the folder within 15 minutes.
settings.climate_rooms_how: One row per widget (Number of widgets, in Advanced). Its type, in the row's dropdown: Temperature (a temperature and a humidity sensor), Air quality (CO₂ and PM2.5), Custom (any two sensors with a unit) or Empty (an empty tile on the Ramka, so the others sit where you want them; empty rows at the end are left out). Settings, in each row: a Temperature widget's comfort ranges, an Air quality widget's limits (the Air page's), a Custom widget's colour. Drag a row by its handle, or use the arrows, to change the order. The n-th widget with a reading is the n-th tile and the n-th line of the charts, in the colour of its dot. An empty name becomes the sensor's area.
settings.about_how: Every Domosenso component this home runs: the lock's, as the last `domosenso render` or `update` left it, and any Home Assistant shows otherwise. Released: the date the catalog released that version.
settings.about_missing: Only the Ramka is listed: `sensor.domosenso_components` is missing. A `domosenso render` with a current `domosenso` command writes it, with every component of the home.
settings.about_related_how: The integrations whose entities the components use, traced from their files.
settings.about_devices_how: The devices behind those entities; firmware and status read live.
settings.about_tagline: Your home on Home Assistant, built with Claude or Codex from parts that already run in a real home.

meta.description: A wall tablet for Home Assistant. A radar wakes it when someone comes into the room; it then rotates through climate, air quality, plants, photos and the home's status, shows what the media player plays, and brings up music, awnings and lights when a hand comes near the screen.

tcl-9469x.description: An 11.5-inch Android tablet (TCL, model 9469X) with a 2200 × 1440 screen.
tcl-9469x.does: Hangs on the wall as the Ramka: the Home Assistant Companion app shows the dashboard full screen, wakes and dims the screen on Home Assistant's commands and reports its light sensor and battery. It stops charging at 80 % by itself, so it can stay on the charger.
